headline: Police Superintendent suspended after testing positive for drugs
summary: AFM Nizam Uddin was suspended by the Home Ministry after a medical screening at a Dhaka hospital revealed the presence of benzodiazepines and amphetamines.
details: A Superintendent of Police (SP), AFM Nizam Uddin, has been suspended following a medical screening at a Dhaka hospital that tested positive for benzodiazepines and amphetamines/methamphetamines.
The suspension was ordered by the Home Ministry under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018, as per a gazette notification issued on September 10.
Nizam was previously attached to the Range DIG Office in Rangpur and had been released from Police Headquarters on January 8 to attend a command and staff course at Mirpur Cantonment.
The drug test occurred after he fell ill on June 7 and was admitted to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Dhaka.
Following the advice of a specialist doctor, a routine medical screening was conducted, which revealed the presence of the controlled substances in his urine samples.
As a result of the positive test, he was declared unfit to continue the Defence Services Command and Staff Course (DSCSC)-2026.
During his suspension, Nizam will receive a subsistence allowance in accordance with government rules.
caption:
A Police Superintendent has been suspended after a medical screening revealed he tested positive for drugs.

A Superintendent of Police (SP), AFM Nizam Uddin, has been suspended following a medical screening at a Dhaka hospital that tested positive for benzodiazepines and amphetamines/methamphetamines.

The suspension was ordered by the Home Ministry under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018, as per a gazette notification issued on September 10.

Nizam was previously attached to the Range DIG Office in Rangpur and had been released from Police Headquarters on January 8 to attend a command and staff course at Mirpur Cantonment.

The drug test occurred after he fell ill on June 7 and was admitted to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Dhaka.

Following the advice of a specialist doctor, a routine medical screening was conducted, which revealed the presence of the controlled substances in his urine samples.

As a result of the positive test, he was declared unfit to continue the Defence Services Command and Staff Course (DSCSC)-2026.

During his suspension, Nizam will receive a subsistence allowance in accordance with government rules.

headline: Local polls likely to start mid-November with UP elections: EC
summary: The Election Commission is planning to begin local government elections from mid-November, starting with Union Parishad polls in phases. The schedule announcement is expected soon.
details: The Election Commission (EC) plans to commence local government elections from mid-November, with Union Parishad polls set to be the first to be held. Election Commissioner Abdur Rahmanel Masud announced this intention today.

Masud stated that if the relevant laws are not amended by that time, the elections will proceed under the existing legal framework. He made these remarks while addressing reporters at the EC headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.

When questioned about the specific timing for the announcement of the election schedule, whether in September or October, Commissioner Masud refrained from providing a definitive date. He indicated that the commission would release the schedule in the near future.
caption:
Local government elections in Bangladesh are likely to commence from mid-November, starting with Union Parishad polls. The Election Commission is preparing to announce the schedule soon.

The Election Commission (EC) plans to commence local government elections from mid-November, with Union Parishad polls set to be the first to be held. Election Commissioner Abdur Rahmanel Masud announced this intention today.

Masud stated that if the relevant laws are not amended by that time, the elections will proceed under the existing legal framework. He made these remarks while addressing reporters at the EC headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.

When questioned about the specific timing for the announcement of the election schedule, whether in September or October, Commissioner Masud refrained from providing a definitive date. He indicated that the commission would release the schedule in the near future.
